title: Tom's cover story
summary: Tom hides a crate in the old ice-house at night. Rook, at his loft window, sees him take a crate in but not where it goes. Next morning Tom lies to Ines and Leo about where he was, and arrives too late to hear the customs news. Rook's half of the truth means he doesn't swallow the lie; Ines does, and passes it to Mira.

crate.truth: Tom hid a crate of Velloran brandy under the sawdust in the old ice-house behind the cooperage.

alibi.truth: (false) Tom says he spent the night at Old Hennick's, mending pots.

customs.truth: A customs cutter is due in Saltmere harbor on Friday to search the cellars.

spine.scene: The net loft over the quay, past midnight

spine.text: Past midnight. Fog off the water. In the net loft over the quay Rook can't sleep. He sits at the little window with his pipe cold in his teeth.

spine.scene: The end of the quay, past midnight, seen from the loft

spine.text: Down the quay a hooded lantern bobs toward the old ice-house behind the cooperage. By the hitch in his walk it's Tom Voss, hauling a crate on a handcart. He shoulders the door open and the lantern goes in.
*To himself.* Out with a cart at this hour. Nothing good.

Inside, Tom sets the lantern on a beam, digs into the old sawdust where the ice blocks used to stand, and lowers the crate into the hollow. The stencil on its lid reads VELLORAN in black. He rakes it over until the crate is under the sawdust and gone.
*Whispering to the dark.* Stay cold, my beauties. Only till Friday.
He hoods the lantern, wheels the empty cart out, and is gone into the fog.
Morning at the Drowned Bell. Ines is wiping tables, Leo is eating porridge at the bar, and Rook nurses a tea by the cold hearth.
News off the mail boat: there's a customs cutter due in on Friday. They'll be turning out every cellar on the coast.
Is that bad for business?
For some business, love.

spine.hint: Rook and Ines talk about the last time the excise men came to Saltmere.

spine.text: Tom comes in yawning, his hair still wet from the pump.
Well, look who's up. Where were you last night? I sent the boy round to your place twice.
Me? I was at Old Hennick's all night, mending pots. Ask anyone. Ask Hennick, if he's sober.
*He says nothing, and watches Tom over his tea.*

spine.hint: Ines teases Tom about his night of pot-mending; Tom embroiders his story.

spine.text: Who's this old man you were with?
Best tinker on the coast, worst drinker. Mends a pot so it rings like a bell.

spine.hint: Tom tries to draw Rook into the joke; Rook won't be drawn.

spine.text: What's wrong with you this morning, Rook? Seen a ghost?
Seen something.

spine.hint: Tom laughs too loudly; Ines notices.

probe.ask: Ines, where was Tom last night?
Tom, where were you last night, really?
Rook, did you see anything odd in the night?
Tom, what's got Ines so worked up this morning?

spine.text: Midday on the quay. Leo finds Rook alone at the fish shed, splicing a rope.
You looked at Tom this morning like he owed you money.
Tom owes everyone money.

spine.hint: Rook decides how much to say to the newcomer.

spine.text: Saw a lantern go into the old ice-house past midnight. Man pushing a cart with a crate on it. Walked like Tom.
At Hennick's all night, he said.
Aye. He said.

spine.hint: Rook says what he thinks of men who lie to Ines.

spine.text: Should we tell her?
Not my cart. Not my business.

spine.hint: Rook goes back to his rope and won't say more.

spine.text: Evening. The Drowned Bell is half full. Mira has come down from the light for lamp oil and sits with her brother. Ines brings them a jug, and Leo joins them.
You look like death, Tom.
He was up all night at Old Hennick's, mending pots, if you'll believe it.
*Flatly.* Hennick hasn't mended a pot since his wife died.
Well, he started again. Late bloomer.

spine.hint: Mira studies her brother; Tom keeps his story going.
Ines brings up the search that's coming at the end of the week, watching Tom's face.

spine.text: I heard the customs cutter is coming Friday.
*He sets down his cup a little hard.* Is it now.

spine.hint: The table talks about the search; Tom says as little as he can.

probe.ask: Mira, where does your brother say he was last night?
Tom, swear to me where you were last night.
Tom, have you heard what's coming on Friday?

spine.text: Tom says he's tired and goes up the lane toward home.
He's lying about something. He always rubs his ear.
He rubs his ear when he's cold, love.

spine.hint: Mira and Ines argue about whether Tom is in trouble again.

spine.text: Mira, does Tom keep things hidden, do you think?
Tom? Debts, under his bed. Feelings, under his debts.

spine.hint: Mira asks Leo why he wants to know; Ines leans in to listen.

spine.text: No reason.

spine.hint: Ines and Mira talk about Tom's scrapes over the years.

probe.ask: Ines, has anyone said where Tom really was?
Rook, what was in the crate, do you reckon?
